title: Processing of identified access data
description: The guest's temporary access code is processed by the Home Hub, which may be linked to the guest's identity through the access event.
assumptions: The access code may be associated with a specific guest account or identity in the system.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system tracks which guest entered which code.

title: Revealing attributes through access code
description: The access code reveals that a guest is attempting to access the home, which is a revealing attribute about the guest's presence and intent.
assumptions: The act of entering an access code inherently reveals the guest's presence at the location.
uncertainty_note: The access code itself may not directly identify the guest, but the action reveals presence.

title: Data type sensitivity - access code collection
description: The temporary access code may be more sensitive than functionally required, as it could be used to identify or track guest access patterns.
assumptions: Access codes could be stored or logged in a way that creates a record of guest access.
uncertainty_note: Depends on how the Home Hub stores and processes the access code.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: The access code may be analyzed, logged, or enriched beyond what is needed for the simple function of unlocking the door.
assumptions: The system may log access events, timestamps, or other metadata beyond the basic unlock function.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the system logs access events for security or audit purposes.

title: Excessive data retention duration
description: Access codes may be retained longer than functionally needed, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: The system may store access code history or logs for extended periods.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the Home Hub's data retention policies.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Guests may not be aware that their access code entry is being logged, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: The system may not provide clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms for access code processing.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard smart home systems may not have explicit privacy disclosures for access codes.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Guests may not have control over how their access code data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: The system may not offer options for guests to control data retention or processing preferences.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the Home Hub system does not provide granular privacy controls for access codes.

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: The motion alert forwarded from Home Hub may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that could be used to link the motion event to a specific individual or device.
assumptions: Motion alerts include device/user identifiers
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion alerts contain identifiable device/user references

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion data combined with timestamp and location context could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals.
assumptions: Motion alerts include timestamp and location context
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion data includes contextual attributes

title: Processing of identified data in motion alert
description: The motion alert may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., device ID, user ID).
assumptions: Motion alerts contain user/device identifiers
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion alerts include identifying references

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion data may reveal revealing attributes such as location, time of activity, and movement patterns that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data includes location and timing information
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion data contains revealing contextual attributes

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data may be more sensitive than needed
description: Motion data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected when strictly required for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Motion data is sensitive personal data
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion data is considered sensitive

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Motion data forwarded to Mobile App Backend may be propagated to other services where it is not functionally needed.
assumptions: Mobile App Backend may share data with other services
uncertainty_note: Assuming backend may propagate data further

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users are not informed about motion data processing
uncertainty_note: Assuming lack of explicit user awareness

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and shared.
assumptions: No user controls for motion data processing

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Assuming data minimization may not be properly enforced

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The motion-detected notification contains the homeowner's unique identifier (e.g., user ID, phone number) to route to the correct device, enabling linking of notification data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Notification includes user identifier for routing

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection data can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns (e.g., when homeowner is home/away, daily routines), enabling inference of personal information.
assumptions: Motion data is collected and stored for analysis

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data (homeowner's identity) to push notifications to the correct device.
assumptions: Notification is tied to specific homeowner account

title: Revealing attributes through motion data
description: Motion detection data reveals revealing attributes such as presence/absence at home, time of activity, which can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data indicates presence patterns

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected, allowing detection of the homeowner's presence/activity through observed communications.
assumptions: Notification is sent when motion is detected

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data
description: Motion detection data may be perceived as highly sensitive (revealing presence patterns) and should only be collected when strictly required for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Motion data is more sensitive than basic notification data

title: Unnecessary processing of motion data
description: Motion data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is necessary to achieve the simple notification functionality.
assumptions: Motion data could be stored/analyzed beyond notification needs

title: Predetermined set of parties receiving data
description: Personal data (motion notification) is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (homeowner) known up front, which is functionally necessary but still represents data exposure.
assumptions: Notification is sent only to registered homeowner

title: Unawareness of motion detection processing
description: Data subjects (homeowners) may not be fully aware that motion detection is active and that their presence patterns are being monitored and processed.
assumptions: Motion detection may be enabled without explicit awareness

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: Homeowners may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how motion data is processed and when notifications are sent.
assumptions: Limited user control over motion detection settings

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion detection data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the notification functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds notification requirements

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip stored in the cloud is identified data associated with a specific homeowner, and is being retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal personal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., location, activities, presence of other individuals) that support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be perceived as more sensitive than other data types, requiring strict handling and access controls.

title: Potential unnecessary video processing
description: The video may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for playback (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, or potentially shared beyond the intended playback functionality.

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing preferences
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or retained.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The video data may contain more personal information than is actually needed for the functional goal of playback, potentially violating data minimization requirements.

title: Video data shared with predetermined parties
description: The video data is made accessible to the homeowner (a predetermined set of parties), which may be more than functionally necessary depending on the access control implementation.
